pages.x: The plague came out of Central Asia along the trade routes of the Mongol world. In 1346 it struck the army of the Golden Horde besieging Caffa, a Genoese port in Crimea. An Italian lawyer wrote that the besiegers hurled the bodies of their dead over the walls.
In October 1347 Genoese galleys put in at Messina in Sicily with sick and dying men on board. Within months the plague was in Genoa, Venice, Marseille and Alexandria, and by 1348 in Paris and London.

Most victims had black swellings, buboes, in the groin or armpit, and died within a week. In the lungs, passed on by coughing, it killed in a day or two. No one knew that fleas from rats carried it. Doctors blamed bad air, or the stars.

Between 1347 and 1351 perhaps a third to a half of all Europeans died, 25 million or more, and millions more in the Middle East and North Africa. In Florence, wrote Boccaccio, the dead were laid in trenches in layers, like goods in a ship's hold.
Many saw God's punishment. Bands of flagellants marched from town to town, whipping themselves bloody to atone for the world's sins, until the pope banned them.

Others looked for someone to blame. Jews were falsely accused of poisoning wells, and were murdered in hundreds of towns: in Strasbourg, on 14 February 1349, some 2,000 were burned. The pope pointed out that Jews were dying of the plague too.

In Boccaccio's Decameron, ten young people flee plague-stricken Florence for a villa in the hills and pass ten days telling each other a hundred stories, funny, sad and rude. It became a founding work of Italian prose.

With so many dead, there were too few hands to work the fields. Peasants and labourers asked for higher wages and moved to find them, despite laws to stop them. In England, anger at those laws and a new tax helped spark the Peasants' Revolt of 1381.

The Black Death came back every few years for three centuries. It shook faith in the Church and in doctors, made the work of ordinary people worth more, and, some historians argue, helped bring the Middle Ages to an end.
